title: Runtime failure prognosis and safe injection playbook
author: Asha Patel
body:
Overview

This playbook defines a reproducible, low‑risk process for prognosing potential runtime failures and running targeted, controlled failure‑injection experiments against the serving runtime. It combines profiling and benchmark signals, scheduler/kernels heuristics, and a strict safety checklist to reduce operator risk and improve our ability to catch regressions before customer impact.

Goals

- Validate that new kernels, scheduling changes, or quantization patches do not introduce cascading failure modes.
- Surface latent failure signatures using low‑blast synthetic probes rather than large‑scale chaos.
- Produce deterministic, debuggable traces that map to kernel, scheduler, and KV cache signals.
- Provide a safe rollback and escalation path with clear ownership.

Scope and when to use this playbook

Use this playbook for:
1. Pre‑merge validation of kernel/scheduler changes that affect eviction, preemption, or admission control.
2. Canary and staged rollout validation for runtime releases touching memory management, KV cache warmstart, or cross‑tenant eviction logic.
3. Profiling investigations where intermittent service degradations are observed but root causes are unclear.

Not covered: multi‑region network partitions (handled by the resilience team runbooks) and hardware BIOS/firmware upgrades (hardware team).

Ownership and roles

- Experiment owner: engineer who creates and runs the injection (must be listed in the experiment ticket).
- Observability lead: runtime profiling owner who configures tracing and ensures required telemetry is captured.
- Oncall liaison: oncall SRE assigned to watch the experiment window and execute rollback if SLOs are violated.
- Reviewer(s): at least one kernel maintainer and one scheduler owner must sign off on the plan.

Safety and risk controls (must pass before any injection)

- Minimum safety checklist: 
  - Production traffic avoided: experiments run in a dedicated staging cohort or a completely sandboxed runtime cluster.
  - Traffic shadowing: production traffic may be shadowed to target without affecting live responses.
  - Blast radius limit: no more than 5% of total capacity in a controlled canary cluster (default).
  - Auto‑abort SLO thresholds: 99th percentile increase > 2x baseline OR error rate delta > 0.5% triggers immediate abort.
  - Observability guards: tracing, kernel telemetry, kvcache epoch counters, per‑slot memory, scheduler credit logs, and GPU thermal metrics must be active.

Experiment design checklist

1. Hypothesis: one sentence describing expected outcome and failure signal (e.g., "A race in eviction will increase KV cache miss rate and cause tail latency spikes in slot 3").
2. Data prerequisites: baseline profiling snapshot and synthetic replay corpus representing target workload.
3. Safety gates: identify abort thresholds and responsible oncall.
4. Trace anchors: list of trace IDs/tags to capture (e.g., experiment_id, slot_id, kernel_variant).
5. Artifact plan: roll forward plan (how to collect traces and artifacts) and rollback plan (revert flag, restart plan).

Concrete injection primitives and examples

- Controlled kernel delay: inject a deterministic 5–50ms kernel execution delay for a specific kernel_id on a single test shard.
- KV cache miss flood: artificially invalidate prefix cache for a cohort to simulate warm‑start pressure.
- Scheduler token drain: reduce admission tokens by X% for a tenant cohort to simulate quota starvation.
- Synthetic memory pressure: allocate transient pinned memory on CUDA for a test container to emulate fragmentation.

Example: kernel delay injection (CLI)

```bash
# create experiment namespace and tag traces
infra-tool experiments create --name "eviction-delay‑probe" --cohort staging-eviction-small --tag experiment_id=evict-delay-2026
# apply 20ms delay to kernel id 0x1f (only on one shard)
infra-tool experiments inject-kernel-delay --kernel 0x1f --delay-ms 20 --shard shard-3 --duration 300s
```

Observability and required telemetry

All experiments must enable the following signals at the sampling rates below: 

| Signal | Minimum sampling | Notes |
|---|---:|---|
| end_to_end_trace | 100% for injected cohort | full trace with step timestamps |
| kernel_exec_histogram | 100% for kernel_id under test | high resolution buckets (0.1ms) |
| kvcache_miss_rate | 10Hz aggregate | per‑epoch granularity |
| slot_latency_p90/p99 | 1s aggregation | baseline compare |
| scheduler_token_balance | 1Hz | correlate with admission attempts |

Profiling guidance and post‑run analysis

- Run with profiler snapshot mode enabled to capture kernel flamegraphs for the period.
- Use the trace correlation table to map high‑latency spans to kernel ids and slot ids.
- Generate a delta report vs baseline containing: p50/p90/p99 latency deltas, kernel latency distribution shift, KV cache miss delta, and scheduler token churn.
- If experiment produces noisy signals, reduce blast radius and iterate — avoid scaling up until signals are consistently reproducible.

Acceptance criteria and decision matrix

- Safe: no SLO trigger, kernel latencies within +/- 10% of baseline, mutational increase in kvcache miss < 2x baseline.
- Degraded (manual review): p99 increase 10–50% OR kvcache miss 2–5x baseline — require reviewer signoff to continue.
- Unsafe (abort): p99 increase > 50% OR error rate delta > specified auto‑abort OR GPU OOM/thermal trip observed — immediate abort and rollback.

Rollback and postmortem steps (ordered)

1. Abort injection via infra tooling and mark experiment status aborted.
2. Execute any automated restarts for affected shards (documented in runbook: runtime-hotpatch-and-quick-redeploy-playbook).
3. Collect and preserve all telemetry artifacts (traces, kernel histograms, kvcache epochs, scheduler logs).
4. Notify oncall rotation and affected owners with a short incident note.
5. Open a postmortem ticket with hypothesis, artifacts, and required followups within 48 hours.

Template: experiment run ticket (minimal fields)

- title: one line summary
- owner: github handle
- cohort: staging cluster name
- hypothesis: one sentence
- injection primitive: kernel_delay/kv_invalidation/scheduler_drain/mem_pressure
- blast_radius: percent or number of shards
- abort_thresholds: p99 delta / error rate delta / OOM indicator
- trace_tags: list
- artifacts_to_collect: list

Example artifact retention policy

- Full traces and kernel histograms: retained for 30 days in object store.
- Aggregated delta reports and dashboards: 90 days.
- Raw profiler snapshots (large): retained 7 days by default; extend retention only with reviewer approval.

Tooling and automation hooks

- infra-tool experiments: create/run/abort (see example above).
- profiler snapshot CLI: profiler snapshot --cohort <cohort> --duration <s> --out /tmp/snap.pb
- telemetry query templates available at: /dashboards/runtime/experiments/templates

Appendix: quick checklist before you press ‘inject’

- [ ] Baseline captured and attached to ticket
- [ ] Observability lead confirmed signal availability and sampling rates
- [ ] Oncall liaison scheduled for experiment window
- [ ] Reviewers signed the plan (kernel + scheduler)
- [ ] Blast radius set and validated in infra tooling
- [ ] Abort thresholds configured in infra-tool and verified
